Glossary

Positive drainage

A roof design condition in which slope is sufficient to drain all water from the roof surface within 48 hours of rainfall under normal conditions.

Template — not yet published Updated July 1, 2026 Editorial standards · Report an error
Template — not yet publishedThis page demonstrates a template structure. It is not editorial content and must not be read as guidance.

Plain-English definition

A roof has positive drainage when water actually leaves it — flowing to drains, scuppers, or gutters — rather than collecting in low spots. It’s the design condition that prevents ponding water.
